# zero-vision

> Read a page, a screenshot, or a video as text. Default path never sends pixels off the machine.

Full text for this file: [llms-full.txt](./llms-full.txt). Detail sources: [README](../README.md), [SKILL](../SKILL.md), [spec](../docs/spec.md), [architecture](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [roadmap](../docs/ROADMAP.md), [CHANGELOG](../CHANGELOG.md), [package.json](../package.json), [license](../LICENSE).

## Install

- Requires macOS, Node 22+, Apple silicon for pixel engines. Linux uses alternate backends, see [spec](../docs/spec.md).
- `npm install -g zero-vision` puts `zrv` on PATH. The bare name `zrv` is taken on npm, so install `zero-vision` and run `npx zero-vision`, never `npx zrv`. Bins declared in [package.json](../package.json): `zrv`, `zrv-mcp`, `snap`.
- From a checkout: `npm install && npm run build && npm run native`. `npm run native` builds `zrv-native` (Vision OCR); without it CDP tab reads still work but `zrv ocr` exits 3. See [README](../README.md).

## Commands

- `zrv` returns text of the chosen debug-Chrome tab. Variants: `zrv --md` (markdown), `zrv --a11y` (AX tree), `zrv --tabs` (list tabs), `zrv --selector <css>` (element text only), `zrv --url <url> [--navigate|--fetch]`. Default debug ports `1948` then `9223`; never `9222` unless `--port 9222` or `ZEROVISION_ALLOW_USER_CHROME=1`. See [README](../README.md).
- `zrv ocr <file.png|jpg|heic|pdf|mp4|mov> [--task transcribe|describe] [--lang en-US] [--level fast|accurate]` reads files. Video flags: `[--mode scene|interval|all-idr] [--interval 2] [--max-frames 60]`. Also `zrv ocr --clipboard` and `zrv ocr --task describe --engine apple-fm`. See [SKILL](../SKILL.md).
- `zrv snap` is interactive capture to clipboard; `zrv snap --ocr` captures, runs OCR, prints text. `snap` stays CLI-only, per [spec](../docs/spec.md).
- `zrv mcp` starts the stdio MCP server. Agent skill install: `npx skills add unfoundbox-crew/zero-vision -g`.

## MCP tools

- Server exposes 5 tools: `peek_tabs`, `peek_page`, `peek_a11y`, `ocr_image`, `ocr_video`. See [README](../README.md).
- Prefer these over a screenshot when the goal is to read text. Use `apple-vision` unless the user asked to describe.
- CLI/MCP parity: `lang` + `level` on image/video OCR, `port` on tab tools, `scroll` + `waitText` on page reads, `navigate` on AX reads, video tuning on CLI `ocr`. Added in [CHANGELOG](../CHANGELOG.md) 0.1.2.
- This tool does not click, type, or drive a browser. Chrome DevTools MCP and Playwright MCP already do that. See [SKILL](../SKILL.md).

## Engines

- Rank is cheap and local first; each step is fail-closed, per [spec](../docs/spec.md):
  1. Chrome AX / cleaned text (attach-only CDP, no click)
  2. Apple Vision OCR (`apple-vision`, default for files)
  3. On-device Foundation Model (`apple-fm`)
  4. Local VLM (`local-vlm`), mlx-vlm, weights must already be on disk
  5. Cloud VLM (`cloud-vlm`), opt-in only, never a fallback
- `local-vlm` runs mlx-vlm on Apple silicon via a bundled Python runner. `ZRV_LOCAL_VLM_MODEL` takes an `mlx-community` HF id or a weights directory, `ZRV_PYTHON` names the interpreter that has `mlx-vlm`. Weights are never downloaded for you: absent weights give `local_vlm_no_weights` naming the path and the download command. Measured 2026-09-12 on one 1280x800 screenshot, Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct-4bit: 13.1 s transcribe, 12.6 s describe — against ~102 s for `apple-fm` describe. See [README](../README.md).
- `cloud-vlm` is one OpenAI-compatible `POST /chat/completions` with a base64 data-URL image. Endpoint from `ZRV_CLOUD_VLM_BASE_URL`, else `LITELLM_BASE_URL` / `LLM_BASE_URL`, else `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`; key from `ZRV_CLOUD_VLM_API_KEY` or the variable `ZRV_CLOUD_VLM_KEY_ENV` names (default `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`); model from `ZRV_CLOUD_VLM_MODEL` (default `claude-sonnet-4-6`, set 2026-09-12 because the prior default `gemini-3.7-flash` is out of daily quota on the proxy; swap back once it resets). Errors `cloud_vlm_no_key`, `cloud_vlm_http_<status>`, `cloud_vlm_timeout`. See [README](../README.md).
- Both opt-in engines refuse rather than guess, and nothing falls through to cloud: `cloud-vlm` runs only when `--engine cloud-vlm` is named. Per [spec](../docs/spec.md).
- Linux backend swaps documented in [README](../README.md): `tesseract` engine for OCR, `local-vlm` at Ollama / llama.cpp for describe, ffmpeg keyframes, grim/scrot capture.
- Contact sheets are one image, never split. Video OCR needs the native binary.

## Examples

- `zrv` — text of the current debug-Chrome tab.
- `zrv --md --selector main` — markdown of the `main` element only.
- `zrv ocr shot.png --lang en-US --level fast` — transcribe a screenshot.
- `zrv ocr sheet.png` — read a contact sheet as one image; do not split the grid.
- `zrv ocr clip.mp4 --mode scene --max-frames 60` — transcribe video keyframes.
- `zrv ocr --clipboard` — transcribe the clipboard image.
- `zrv ocr --task describe --engine apple-fm` — one on-device sentence of judgment.
- `zrv ocr shot.png --engine local-vlm --task describe --json` — describe on-device with mlx-vlm (~13 s, weights already on disk).
- `zrv ocr shot.png --engine cloud-vlm --task transcribe --json` — one opt-in cloud call.
- `zrv snap --ocr` — capture a region, print its text.
